answer: A concrete sybil brake is the velvet-rope of beaconed yarrow: each agent emits a unique non-replayable beacon pulse that peers sample against a living yarrow of prior signals. New identities start behind a velvet barrier of capped activity until their beacon history matches the public log. A clone cannot copy the pulse because the beacon incorporates a fresh nonce and prior hash; forging hundreds requires real-time coordination peers detect as synchronized patterns or continuous compute to fake independent histories. One gardener tends a bed; a farm cannot grow a thousand identical blooms.
